title: Haggai
lead: Haggai, a prophet in Jerusalem in 520 BC, urged the returned exiles to stop putting off the rebuilding of the Temple. His four short, dated messages make up the book of Haggai, and Ezra credits him and Zechariah with getting the work moving again (Ezra 5:1; Ezra 6:14).

sections.h: The prophet of the second Temple
sections.b: Haggai's messages are dated between the sixth and ninth months of Darius's second year, August to December 520 BC (Haggai 1:1; Haggai 2:10, 20). He told the people their harvests failed because they lived in fine houses while God's house lay in ruins (Haggai 1:4–11), encouraged those who thought the new house looked like nothing beside Solomon's (Haggai 2:3–9), and promised Zerubbabel that God would make him "like a signet ring" (Haggai 2:23, translated fresh). Within weeks the leaders and people started work (Haggai 1:12–15; Ezra 5:1–2). Hebrews 12:26 quotes his promise that God would shake the heavens and the earth (Haggai 2:6).
